title: Reagan: The Life
author: H.W. Brands
target_audience: Readers interested in American presidential history
Scholars and students of political science
General audience seeking insight into Ronald Reagan’s life and influence
Fans of comprehensive biographies and historical analysis
core_themes: American conservatism and the shifting political landscape
The Cold War and foreign policy
primary_purpose: To offer a thorough and balanced account of Ronald Reagan’s life, exploring his impact as a leader, the complexities of his character, and his enduring influence on American society and world affairs.

structure_format.organization: Divided into chapters following Reagan's life from childhood through presidency and post-presidency years
features: Analysis of Reagan's policies and legacy

key_concepts_lessons: The making of a political persona can be as important as policy substance.
Reagan’s optimism and ability to communicate shaped national sentiment and identity.
Leadership involves both image-making and behind-the-scenes decision-making.
Cold War strategies included not just military build-up, but also negotiation and soft power.
The complexities and contradictions of Reagan’s conservatism and its long-term effects.
style_tone: Balanced—neither hagiographic nor critical for its own sake
notable_features: Conveys both Reagan’s personal side and public persona
Balanced judgments, aiming to separate myth from reality
Integration of Reagan's Hollywood career, governorship, and presidency
Situates Reagan within the broader sweep of 20th-century American history
Relies on new research and previously unpublished sources
cultural_historical_context: Written in the 2010s, with benefit of declassified material and hindsight on Reagan’s long-term impact; Reagan’s legacy continued to shape American politics and conservative identity into the 21st century.
reception_impact: Acclaimed for narrative skill and even-handedness
Noted for synthesizing vast material into a compelling story
Praised as one of the best single-volume Reagan biographies
Sources commend the book’s approachability for both experts and lay readers
Some critics note it favors breadth over exhaustive policy analysis
comparable_titles: Reagan: An American Journey by Bob Spitz
Dutch: A Memoir of Ronald Reagan by Edmund Morris
President Reagan: The Role of a Lifetime by Lou Cannon
The Age of Reagan by Sean Wilentz
